items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Yeah or Bix or — ... I mean maybe they listen to Duke, maybe they listen to Bix and the older guys or whatever

ctx.x: We were having a discussion with a few people today about traditional jazz and they feel it’s not well represented in the jazz education scene. And I’m trying to figure out why. Why is the music of Charlie Parker and John Coltrane given more artistic weight than, you know the music of Jean Goldkette or —
Or Bix or that kind of thing.
